title: EQT acquisition of Range Resources creates America's largest natural gas producer
gist: EQT's all-stock acquisition of Range Resources (combined EV above US$50bn) creates America's largest gas producer at over 9 Bcfe/d, which Wood Mackenzie sees as a bet on demand-pull from power generation and data centres, with US$325m baseline synergies.

insights.claim: EQT's all-stock acquisition of Range Resources creates a combined enterprise value above US$50 billion and a producer above 9 Bcfe/d, about 25% larger than its nearest rival.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Creates the dominant Appalachian gas producer; scale peers may respond with consolidation.

insights.claim: The combined EQT-Range will produce roughly three times more than most gas-focused peers.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Scale advantage in costs and market access versus smaller gas producers.

insights.claim: Range shareholders receive 0.987 EQT shares per Range share, a 21% premium; EQT holders will own about 73% and Range holders 27%, with closing expected in Q1 2027 subject to approvals.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Defines merger-arb terms and timeline; regulatory and shareholder votes are the risks.

insights.claim: EQT has completed more than US$12 billion of acquisitions since 2023, making Appalachian consolidation a continuing strategy.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Acquisitive track record suggests further deals are possible.

insights.claim: North American gas markets have shifted from producer-push to demand-pull, and the deal positions EQT as supplier of choice for Appalachian power generation and data centre growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Frames gas equities as a derivative of power and AI-load demand rather than supply-driven.
insights.quote: North American gas markets have shifted from producer-push to demand-pull

insights.claim: Range adds scale, inventory and liquids diversification, with NGLs and oil about 30% of its production, giving the combined company a more liquids-rich profile.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Some liquids exposure diversifies pure-gas price risk.
insights.locator: A high-quality and strategically complementary asset

insights.claim: Range drilled the first Marcellus gas well in 2004 and has stayed focused on south-west Pennsylvania, while EQT was already the largest Marcellus producer.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Deepens EQT's inventory concentration in the core Marcellus.
insights.locator: A high-quality and strategically complementary asset

insights.claim: EQT and Range both command premium valuations relative to gas-focused peers because investors reward low costs, infrastructure ownership and exposure to future demand growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Low cost, owned infrastructure and demand exposure are the valuation drivers to screen for in gas equities.

insights.claim: EQT cut net debt from over US$12 billion after the Equitrans Midstream acquisition to US$5.5 billion by Q2 2026, giving it capacity for another large deal.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Deleveraging preceded the deal; leverage on the combined entity is a watch item.
insights.locator: Timing, balance sheet and synergy targets

insights.claim: EQT chose transformative scale over buybacks, a strategy that has not prioritised short-term shareholder returns, and Wood Mackenzie expects the market to reward that discipline given strengthening demand.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Supports a growth-over-returns re-rating case, though it defers cash returns.

insights.claim: EQT targets US$325 million of annual baseline synergies within two years plus more than US$300 million of longer-term development upside, and beat synergy guidance on its last two major deals.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Track record lends credibility; monitor delivery versus targets.
insights.locator: Timing, balance sheet and synergy targets
